subtitle: Long noun phrases, and participial clauses
words.intro: Berlin’s Museum Island holds five museums on one bit of land in the Spree. Its labels are small masterpieces: a whole civilisation in one sentence, with the verb somewhere near the fire exit.

grammar[0].blocks[2].title: Shorten a chain
grammar[0].blocks[2].text: *die Ergebnisse der Studie des Instituts* → *die Ergebnisse der Institutsstudie*. Two genitives in a row is the limit.
grammar[0].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[0].fact: Museum labels in German have grown shorter since they began being written by people who’d watched visitors read them. The average visitor spends a few seconds on a label. Long noun chains were once considered a sign of respect for the reader, and in some places they still are.

grammar[1].fact: You’ll see this one chiefly in literature, and a little in the press: *Vom Lärm geweckt, stand er auf.* In speech nobody says it unless they mean to sound like a novel. Used once in an essay, it’s elegant. Used twice, it’s a parody.

listen.intro: A talk with many details. Listen for the long noun phrases and say what each is really about: find the head.

document.intro: A real label beside a small carving in a German museum. It’s beautifully clear, for a label. Find the head of each long noun phrase, and notice the joke in the very last sentence.
document.fact: Labels are often written by several people and approved by committee. So the small joke at the end of this one, about the apples, may have taken some fighting for.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Write the head noun of each phrase.
reading.intro: Maya’s friend Paula works as a junior curator. A label for a new exhibition has to be ready by five, and it’s Paula’s job to write it. Her boss, Frau Prof. Sommer, the head of the department, has come to read it. It’s long, but so is the history of the object.
reading.photos[1].caption: Im Humboldt Forum: Woher kommen diese Figuren, und wem gehören sie?
reading.fact: The bust of Nefertiti was found in 1912 by a team under Ludwig Borchardt, and it has been in Berlin since 1913, apart from war years. Egypt has been asking for it back for about a century. Berlin has returned other objects, including bronzes to Nigeria in 2022. Labels have been changing, often in the direction of more verbs.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Rewrite each one with subject and verb.

reading.tasks[1].items[1].answer: Besucher fotografieren sie oft. Sie steht im Saal.
